story:
As your gaze falls upon this exquisite Etched Silver and Glass Hookah Base, imagine an evening under a starlit Udaipur sky, over a century ago. Crafted around the 1890s, this magnificent piece is a testament to royal leisure, where heavy, bell-shaped, mouth-blown lead glass met the intricate artistry of sterling silver platework. Each delicate floral etching whispers tales of verdant palace gardens, where maharajas and maharanis once reclined, enjoying perfumed tobacco amidst laughter and gentle breezes.

This isn't merely a decorative item; it's a tangible piece of our city's soul. The detailed artistry speaks volumes of the skilled metalworkers who graced these very palaces, creating objects not just of function, but of profound beauty and status. It symbolizes an era of refined indulgence and social grace, making it a priceless fragment of Udaipur's opulent heritage, forever echoing the whispers of royal garden assemblies within these historic walls.
handlingNotes: Subject is glass heavy bottom. Do not lift hookah by metal collars alone; support glass body base from underneath when carrying.
